classification.difficultyReason: Composite figures require triangle angle sums, supplementary angles and equal base angles.

content.prompt: Determine the value represented by the pronumeral. You do not need to show working out.

spec.description: Triangle with two internal apex-to-base segments, an apex unknown, a 12-degree apex sector with a leader, and a dashed rightward base extension.
spec.mathematics: The left base angle is 48 degrees. The angle to the right of the first internal segment at its base is 114 degrees. The sector between the second internal segment and the right outer side is 12 degrees. The exterior angle at the right base endpoint is 155 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied measurements remain visible; the value of x is omitted.

answer.worked:
The angle on the left of the first internal segment at the base is $180^\circ-114^\circ=66^\circ$ (angles on a straight line).
$$\begin{align*}x+48+66&=180\\x+114&=180\\x&=66^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of a triangle.

spec.description: Unlettered composite figure with a junction on its straight upper edge, two segments from the junction to the lower vertices, two right-angle markers and matching single side ticks.
spec.mathematics: At the lower-left vertex, the upper-left side is perpendicular to the junction segment, and the adjacent angle is 53 degrees. At the lower-middle vertex, the lower-left side is perpendicular to the junction segment. The lower-middle-to-junction and junction-to-right segments are equal. The right endpoint angle is 35 degrees. The straight angle above the junction is labelled 180 degrees; a is the sector between the upper-left and lower-left rays from the junction.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied measurements and structural marks remain visible; the value of a is omitted.

answer.worked:
In the central right triangle, the angle at the junction is $180^\circ-90^\circ-53^\circ=37^\circ$.
The right-hand triangle is isosceles, so both base angles are $35^\circ$. Its angle at the junction is $180^\circ-35^\circ-35^\circ=110^\circ$.
The three angles below the straight upper edge sum to $180^\circ$:
$$\begin{align*}a+37+110&=180\\a+147&=180\\a&=33^\circ\end{align*}$$
